# Introduction

## Introduction

In the following presentation our idea is to share the way the Density Matrix (DM) model works, using it for a real case study.

## Case study - Palmer Penguins

We will be working with the Palmer `penguins` dataset, which is a well-known dataset in the R community for classification tasks. The goal is to classify penguin species based on various features. The `penguins` dataset is as follows:

```{r DM-presentation-1, echo=FALSE}
Data <- modeldata::penguins
Data %>% glimpse()
```

## Case study - Palmer Penguins

Our objective, therefore, is to identify the species using all the other variables as predictors. The species are Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo.

<img src="https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/lter_penguins.png" width="600px"/>

# Data preparation

## Data preparation - Species selection

However, due to the limitations of our model so far, we will be working with only 2 of those species: Adelie and Gentoo, the ones whose difference in `Body mass` and `Flipper length` can allow us to separate them more easily.

```{r DM-presentation-2}
Data %<>% 
  filter(species != "Chinstrap") %>%
  mutate(y = ifelse(species == "Adelie", "0", "1"), .keep = "unused") %>%
  mutate(y = factor(y)) %>% 
  relocate(y)
```

## Data preparation - aNAlysis

We will just drop the `NA` values.

```{r DM-presentation-3}
Data %<>% na.omit()
```

## Data preparation - Number of Categories

```{r DM-presentation-4, echo = FALSE}
source(here("R/plot_n_levels.R"))
plot_n_levels(Data)
```

# Data preparation - Factor order fix

Initially, the `y` variable has levels "0" and "1". We will change the order so that "1" is the positive level, so we don't have to recode the whole model.

```{r DM-presentation-5}
Data %<>% mutate(y = forcats::fct_relevel(y, "1", "0"))
```

## Data preparation - split

For the sake of comparison, we will split the data into a training set and a test set, using a proportion defined in the parameters section. We will stratify the split based on the `species` variable to ensure that both species are represented proportionally in both sets.

```{r DM-presentation-6}
Data_split <- Data %>% rsample::initial_split(prop = 1 - params$test_prop, strata = "y")
Data_train <- Data_split %>% rsample::training()
Data_test <- Data_split %>% rsample::testing()
train_resamples <- bootstraps(Data_train, times = params$bootstrap_size)
```

# Workflow

## Workflow

## 🤖 Models

```{r DM-presentation-7, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RodGal-2020/ML_common/refs/heads/main/models/classification.R")
# Models is a named list, and we just want to keep those that we can actually use
models %<>% magrittr::extract(c("rf", "knn"))
require(ranger) # For rf
```

## 📊 Metrics

```{r DM-presentation-8}
my_metrics = metric_set(bal_accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, ppv, npv, accuracy, f_meas, kap, mcc)
```

## 🍳 Recipes (1/2)

We just want an easy and scalable example, so we will define a simple recipe that only removes zero-variance and near-zero variance predictors. We will not apply any other transformation, as we want to see how the models behave with the raw data.

```{r DM-presentation-9}
rec_basic <- recipe(y ~ ., data = Data_train) %>%
  # step_novel(all_predictors()) %>% # Valores nuevos, aunque no se den
  # step_other(all_predictors(), threshold = 0.01, other = "other") %>% # Categorías infrecuentes
  # step_novel(all_predictors()) %>%
  # step_dummy(all_nominal(), -y) %>%
  # themis::step_smote(y, over_ratio = 0.5) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_nzv(all_predictors()) # Near zero
```

## 🍳 Recipes (2/2)

Knowing that we will be working with categorical variables, we define a very simple recipe that we will later apply to generate a dataset suitable for the DM.

```{r DM-presentation-10}
rec_dm <- recipe(y ~ ., data = Data_train) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_nzv(all_predictors())
```

## Data baking - Common

```{r DM-presentation-12, echo=FALSE}
(Data_baked <- rec_basic %>% prep(Data) %>% bake(new_data = Data))
```

## Data baking - DM

For comparison, we will also bake the data using the DM recipe, both for training and test sets.

```{r DM-presentation-13, echo=FALSE}
(Data_baked_dm <- rec_dm %>% prep(Data_train) %>% bake(new_data = Data_train) %>% mutate(test = FALSE) %>% 
  bind_rows(Data_test %>% mutate(test = TRUE)) %>% relocate(y, test))
```

```{r DM-presentation-13, echo=FALSE}
Data_baked_train_dm <- rec_dm %>% prep(Data_train) %>% bake(new_data = Data_train)
Data_baked_test_dm <- rec_dm %>% prep(Data_test) %>% bake(new_data = Data_test)
```

## Data baking - DM - SMOTE effect

Here we would see the effect of SMOTE if we had applied it in the recipe. We can see how the classes are balanced in the training set.

```{r DM-presentation-14 }
dim(Data_baked) / dim(Data_baked_dm)
```

# Tuning

## 🔧 workflowset

```{r DM-presentation-11}
all_workflows <- workflow_set(
  preproc = list("rec_basic" = rec_basic),
  models = models) %>%
  option_add(grid = params$grid_size, strict = FALSE)
```

## Tuning

```{r DM-presentation-11}
all_workflows %<>% workflow_map(
  resamples = train_resamples,
  metrics = my_metrics,
  verbose = TRUE
) %>%
  mutate(wflow_id = sub("rec_basic_", "", wflow_id)) # Eliminamos "formula_" en cada identificador
```

## Best model - Final parameters

We must "finalize" the model tuning first, to then be able to access the final parameters used in each of them.

```{r DM-presentation-20, echo = FALSE}
wflow_ids = all_workflows %>% pull(wflow_id)

tuning_results <- wflow_ids %>%
  map(~ extract_workflow_set_result(all_workflows, id = .x))

# We filter those that actually obtained results, something important when working
# with the test version of the file
drop_me = c()
for (model in 1:length(tuning_results)) {
  NA_metric = tuning_results[[model]]$.metrics[[1]] %>%
    filter(.metric == params$rank_metric) %$%
    .estimate %>%
    is.na() %>%
    all()

  if (NA_metric) {
    drop_me %<>% c(model)
  }
}

if (!is.null(drop_me)) {
  tuning_results[[drop_me]] <- NULL
  wflow_ids = wflow_ids[-drop_me]
  model_names = wflow_ids
}

tuning_results %<>%
  map(~ select_best(.x, metric = params$rank_metric)) %>%
  set_names(wflow_ids) %>%
  imap(
    ~ .x %>% mutate(wflow_id = .y)
  ) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  select(-.config) %>%
  rename(model = wflow_id) %>%
  relocate(model) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>%
  # Everything which is not "model" now is a parameter
  pivot_longer(cols = -model, names_to = "param", values_to = "value") %>%
  arrange(model) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(value = round(as.numeric(value), 3) %>% as.character)

```


# DM

## DM - Comparable Error Estimation

To ensure fair comparison, we use the same workflow as in the previous workflow:

1. Prepare the recipe with `Data_train` and apply it to both training and test sets.  
2. **Train manually** on `Data_train` using `train_resamples()`.  
3. Predict on `Data_test`.  
4. Compute error with `my_metrics()`.

This keeps the `dm()` evaluation consistent with all other models.

```{r DM-presentation-22 }
# Función para aplicar el modelo dm a cada muestra de bootstrap
aplicar_dm <- function(resample) {
  # resample$splits es el objeto que contiene las particiones de datos
  # resample = train_resamples$splits[[1]]

  data_resample_train <- rsample::analysis(resample) %>%   # extrae los datos de entrenamiento de la muestra bootstrap
    mutate(test = FALSE)
  data_resample_test <- rsample::assessment(resample) %>%
    mutate(test = TRUE)

  data_resample <- bind_rows(data_resample_train, data_resample_test)  # une los datos de entrenamiento y test

  modelo <- dm(data_resample, n_breaks = 3, objective_var = "y", verbose = 0, test_var = "test")  # aplica tu modelo
  return(modelo)  # devuelve el modelo o resultados (predicciones, métricas, etc.)
}

# train_resamples$splits[[1]] %>% aplicar_dm()
dms <- map(train_resamples$splits, aplicar_dm)

# Fix codification of the levels of the factor variables
# Example of the error:
#
# rsample::assessment(train_resamples$splits[[1]])$y %>% table()
# dms[[1]]$.truth %>% table()
# dms[[1]]$.truth %>% head()
#
# When launching dm 1s turned to 1s and 0s to 2s. We fix that using the forcats package:
dms %<>% map(
  ~ .x %>%
    mutate(across(c(.pred, .truth), ~ forcats::fct_recode(.x, "0" = "2")))
)

dm_metrics <- dms %>% map(
  ~ .x %>% my_metrics(
    # Que tengan los mismos niveles como factores, asumiendo que en .truth están
    mutate(.pred = factor(.pred, levels = levels(.truth))),
    truth = .truth, estimate = .pred
  )
)

# Ahora combinamos los resultados anteriores, promediando para cada métrica
dm_metrics <- dm_metrics %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  group_by(.metric) %>%
  summarise(.estimate = mean(.estimate))

```

## Density functions visualization

Podemos representar las funciones de densidad de probabilidad para cada una de las clases, para cada uno de los grupos considerados:

```{r DM-presentation-25, echo=FALSE}
library(ks)
```

```{r DM-presentation-26, echo=FALSE}
plot_class = function(class_value, new_title, show_plot = TRUE, save_dir = NULL) {
  # class_value = 0
  data <- dms %>% 
  bind_rows() %>% 
  filter(.truth == class_value) # Filter for the class

  # KDE estimation
  H <- Hpi(x = data[, c("r", "phi_1")]) # Bandwidth matrix estimation
  fhat <- kde(x = data[, c("r", "phi_1")], H = H, gridsize = c(100, 100)) # KDE with ks
  
  # Convert the KDE output to a data frame
  density_data <- expand.grid(
    r = fhat$eval.points[[1]], 
    phi_1 = fhat$eval.points[[2]]
  ) %>%
    mutate(density = as.vector(fhat$estimate))
  
  # Plot the KDE-based heatmap
  kde_plot <- ggplot(density_data, aes(x = r, y = phi_1, fill = density)) +
    geom_tile() +
    labs(
      title = new_title,
      subtitle = "Kernel Density Estimate",
      x = expression(r),
      y = expression(phi[1])
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c() + # Add a visually appealing color scale
    theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") # Remove the legend
  
  if (show_plot) {
    print(kde_plot)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(save_dir)) {
    ggsave(filename = paste0(save_dir, "/kde_plot_", class_value, ".png"), plot = kde_plot)
  }
}
```

```{r DM-presentation-27 }
plot_class(1, new_title = "(a) Not diagnosed", show_plot = FALSE, save_dir = here::here("figs"))
```

```{r DM-presentation-28 }
plot_class(2, new_title = "(b) Diagnosed", show_plot = FALSE, save_dir = here::here("figs"))
```

# Comparison

Everything is in `dm_metrics`.

```{r DM-presentation-32, echo=FALSE}
metrics_dmm <- dmm_metrics %>%
  select(.metric, .estimate) %>%
  mutate(wflow_id = "dmm", rank = 0)

metrics_others <- all_workflows %>%
  rank_results(rank_metric = params$rank_metric, select_best = TRUE) %>% # Ordenados según accuracy
  select(.metric, mean, wflow_id, rank) %>%
  rename(.estimate = mean)

metrics_full <- bind_rows(metrics_dmm, metrics_others) %>% arrange(rank) %>%
  mutate(.estimate = round(.estimate, 3))

metrics_table <- metrics_full %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = .estimate) %>%
  select(-rank) %>%
  relocate(wflow_id, f_meas, accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, kap) %>%
  arrange(-f_meas) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

# Test comparison

## Test comparison

We want to compare the results obtained with the different models, including the DM, on the test set. To do so, we have to end the tuning process and obtain the predictions on the test set, for both the ML and the DM approaches.

## ML

```{r DM-presentation-35 }
results = list()
wks = list()
fits = list()
preds = Data_test %>% select(y)
test_metrics = tibble()

if (!"rec_basic_tree" %in% all_workflows$wflow_id) {
  # Add rec_basic to all workflows names
  all_workflows %<>% mutate(wflow_id = paste0("rec_basic_", wflow_id))
}

for (model_name in model_names) {
  # Recuperamos el modelo resultante para cada modelo del workflow,
  # nos quedamos con el mejor y...
  results[[model_name]] <- all_workflows %>%
    extract_workflow_set_result(paste0("rec_basic_", model_name))
  wks[[model_name]] <- all_workflows %>%
    extract_workflow(paste0("rec_basic_", model_name))
  
  best_rank_metric <- select_best(results[[model_name]], metric = params$rank_metric)
  
  # finalizamos el ajuste
  fits[[model_name]] <- wks[[model_name]] %>% 
    finalize_workflow(best_rank_metric) %>%
    # finalize_workflow(tibble(prod_degree = 1)) %>%
    fit(data = Data_train)
  
  # Now the new predictions
  preds %<>% bind_cols(
    !!model_name := predict(fits[[model_name]], Data_test) %>% pull(1)
  )
  
  # Now, for each combination, we obtain our metrics
  test_metrics %<>% 
    bind_rows(
      my_metrics(preds, truth = y, estimate = !!model_name) %>%
        mutate(wflow_id = model_name)
    )
}
```

### Renaming

```{r DM-presentation-36 }
test_metrics %<>%
  # We want to change like follows:
  # RF <- rf
  # Logistic Regression <- logistic
  # SVM-P <- svm_p
  # SVM-R <- svm_r
  # CART <- cart
  # XGB <- xgb
  # Tree <- tree
  # NN <- nn
  # Bag CART <- bag_cart
  # KNN <- knn
  mutate(wflow_id = case_when(
     wflow_id == "rf" ~ "RF",
     wflow_id == "logistic" ~ "Logistic Regression",
     wflow_id == "svm_p" ~ "SVM-P",
     wflow_id == "svm_r" ~ "SVM-R",
     wflow_id == "cart" ~ "CART",
     wflow_id == "xgb" ~ "XGB",
     wflow_id == "tree" ~ "Tree",
     wflow_id == "nn" ~ "NN",
     wflow_id == "bag_cart" ~ "Bag CART",
     wflow_id == "knn" ~ "KNN",
     TRUE ~ wflow_id
    )
   ) %>% 
  relocate(wflow_id)
```

## dm

Queremos ajustar aquí la dm sobre todo el conjunto y luego aplicarla únicamente al conjunto test, para obtener las mismas métricas. Necesitaremos los archivos `dm.R` para esto.

```{r DM-presentation-37 }
dm_metrics_test <- dm(Data, n_breaks = 3, objective_var = "y", verbose = 0, test_var = "test") %>%   
  my_metrics(
    mutate(.pred = factor(.pred, levels = levels(.truth))),
    truth = .truth, estimate = .pred
  )

metrics_dm <- dm_metrics_test %>%
  select(.metric, .estimate) %>%
  mutate(wflow_id = "dm")

test_metrics <- test_metrics %>%
  bind_rows(metrics_dm)
```
